summary: Repeated the full migration request; prior reply missed it
detailed_context: Nick's current message restates his earlier request almost word for word: commit all changes, retire PAI, make every ~/dev repo self-sufficient for plain Claude Code, with hard limits and a step-by-step plan. The previous response was an AccessBuddy payment-required verification report, which does not address the migration at all, and it is truncated mid-deliverable. Asking for the same task again signals that the earlier reply missed it, which fits the 'repeated request' pattern (2-3). The restated constraints (no ~/.claude changes, no deletions, no secrets, no pushes, work on branches) suggest he expects closer adherence next time. Lesson: when a message repeats a prior request, treat the earlier reply as a miss and start the requested steps directly, with Step 0 (locate the life-os source) and Step 1 (map repos under ~/dev) first.
